workload: One 8-channel, 60 s, 16 kHz float32 array (a CHiME/AMI-style array chunk); SNR mixing calls audio_energy on that reference track.
notes: np.average(audio**2) materializes a full-size float32 square (~30.7 MiB here) and reduces it to a scalar. A chunked multiply into a small buffer, reduced with the same pairwise float32 sum, removes that temporary and can keep the returned energy bit-identical. Overlap: lhotse/audio/mixer.py is in no open PR and in no PR merged since 2026-10-13; dexhunter's PRs (#1613, #1636, #1638, #1654, #1655) do not touch it. No open issue marks it deprecated or mid-refactor.

workload: Mix one minute of 8-channel 16 kHz audio with a mono noise track at 10 dB SNR; this is MixedCut.load_audio for an array recording.
notes: A mono track mixed into 8 channels is np.tile'd to (8, T) before the add, so the call's extra peak is the output plus a second full buffer (~61.5 MiB, of which ~30.7 MiB is the tile). Adding the (1, T) track with broadcasting is bit-identical and drops that tile. Overlap: same file as audio_energy, untouched by open PRs and by PRs merged since 2026-10-13. Open mixing PRs are on lhotse/cut/mixed.py and lhotse/dataset/collation.py, not AudioMixer. dexhunter has no PR on this file.

workload: Soft-clip (+6 dB, normalized) one minute of 8-channel 16 kHz audio, as load_audio does when a Clipping transform is attached.
notes: The body allocates an abs() buffer, then a new array for divide, multiply, tanh, divide, multiply, and a final .copy(). Extra peak is ~92.5 MiB against a 30.7 MiB result. Writing those ufuncs into one out= buffer is bit-identical and leaves a single result buffer. Overlap: lhotse/augmentation/clipping.py is in no open PR and has no commit since 2026-10-13. dexhunter's PRs do not touch it. No open issue says clipping is being refactored or removed.

workload: Downsample one 8-channel, 30 s, 48 kHz recording to 16 kHz with the dataloader sinc kernel.
notes: conv1d on all 8 channels at once holds a workspace of ~317 MiB for a 15.4 MiB result (41-tap kernel). Running the same kernel one channel at a time is torch.equal to the batched call and cuts the extra peak to about 52 MiB. Overlap: lhotse/augmentation/resample.py is in no open PR and has no commit since 2026-10-13. Recent resampling edits are in lhotse/audio/backend.py, lhotse/audio/recording.py, and lhotse/augmentation/torchaudio.py, not this kernel. dexhunter's PRs do not touch it. The file is the stable vendored sinc kernel.
